The purpose of the Palme Centers monitoring is to ensure that the programme teams have as accurate information as possible about outcomes, to enable well-founded analysis and learnings. The analysis and learnings shall facilitate the ongoing adaptation and improvement of the programmes and continuously test the relevance of the programmes idea on how change happen. Contextually relevant and cost-effective programmes are essential for being accountable to the rights holders. Furthermore, the analysis and learning are important to be able to create qualitative financial and narrative reports, which help us to be accountable towards the board and the donors. Finally, gathering information about the outcomes of the programmes is very helpful when communicating what the Palme Center does and contributes to. The project includes monitoring travels and related costs.

There is a budget for evaluation within each of the six operational programmes in order to tailor the evaluations to the specific contexts and focus issues of the programmes. Evaluations on an overall level will be conducted within the methods programme. The lessons drawn from evaluations will inform decisions and planning regarding ongoing interventions. The costs for evaluations are divided equally between the years but will most likely be conducted later in the programme period.Project OrganisationsThe project is implemented by the Palme Center.Project ObjectiveTo evaluate outcomes/behavioural changes in relation to programme objectives and to draw lessons learned which will inform decisions and planning regarding ongoing interventions.

The project is implemented in South Africa. The main outcome areas it contributes to are gender equality and democracy and human rights. The main rights holders are women, youth and elderly people. Through counselling, workshops and campaigns the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.

The local offices of the Palme Center is a vital part of our work and operations and is established in a number of countries based on a strategic decision to increase presence to meet our operational needs.

The aim of the project is to strengthen the capacity of the partner organisations within the programme, enable collaboration, networking and exchange, follow up and reflect on the programme framework to facilitate any necessary adaptation.
Pre-studies aim to carry out feasibility assessments at an early stage of possible projects, operations and/or partners to support.

OPC applies a zero-tolerance policy on corruption. It is in this premise that capacity building is the central point of its efforts and initiatives with focus on strengthening accountability, participation and transparency among its partner-organisations and member-organisations. The project focuses on the conduct of regular and up-to-date anti-corruption seminars such as fraud awareness/detection and strengthening existing partner-organisations finance and administrative system. Part of OPC's anti-corruption policy is the inclusion of procurement and code of conduct steering documents that are regularly revisited and form part of all cooperation agreements. In addition to developing system and procedures to counter corruption, there is a specific focus on awareness raising with regards to nepotism, cronyism and power relations. OPC's work in this regard is centered around values and expected behaviour rather than a list of consequences related to specific transgressions.Project OrganisationsThis is a Palme Center project.Other Donors to the OrganisationNo other donors involved in this project.Project ObjectiveThe main objective of the project is to contribution in the fight against corruption by establishing, supporting and contributing to changes, more transparent and democratic organisational structures and behavioural patterns. OPC believes that the labour movement and civil society have a central role to play as role models, democractic schools and agents of change in the work against corruption.

SummaryThe project is implemented in South Africa. The main outcome areas it contributes to are democracy and human rights, equality and worker´s rights and gender equality. The main rights holders are rural women, migrant women, small scale producers,  farm workers and farm dwellers. Through trainings, study circles and dialogues the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between TCOE and ABF Skaraborg, a branch of The Workers´Educational Association (ABF).Trust for Community Outreach and Education (TCOE) works with rural poor in Eastern Cape and Western Cape, especially regarding the right to and redistribution of land. TCOE also collaborates with a number of small agricultural organizations with a membership base of over 15,000 people in order to support their self-sufficiency and their political capabilities. As a result of its close cooperation with the agricultural collective, TCOE has established itself as a voice in the discussion on the design of the land reform and related policy.ABF is Sweden's largest adult education association. ABF offers study circles, courses, lectures and cultural events for about 750,000 people annually.
